title: {Syn} The Prime Number Theorem as a Density Map
content:
The prime number theorem says that the number of primes up to x is approximately x divided by log x. In plain language, primes thin out, but they thin out with a very specific rhythm.

This is why a random large integer near x has about a 1/log x chance of being prime. The theorem turns a jagged counting function into a reliable large-scale forecast.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
